[mpadre] @MaxHashrate: Not sure what point you're trying to make. The Indian automotive industry is much bigger than you seem to think. The vast majority of cars sold in India are manufactured or assembled locally, including vehicles from international brands like Toyota. In fact, even the Toyota Camry is assembled in India for domestic use.
For perspective, the Camry costs approximately A$76,000 when converting its Indian ex-showroom price, whereas a Suzuki Fronx, which is far more representative of India's mass-market automotive industry, starts at around A$10,800.
And it's not as though Indians don't support their own brands. Mahindra is hugely popular among Indians migrants, yet how often do we see people making fun of or looking down on Mahindra vehicles? Every oZbargain thread about Mahindra vehicles is filled with racist comments.
There's also a side of the industry people overlook. India's automotive component industry exported approximately US$22.9 billion worth of components. That's billions of dollars' worth of automotive parts supplied to global markets, with Indian-made components finding their way into vehicles manufactured and assembled around the world, including by international automotive brands.
If you're referring to Indians in Australia driving Toyota Camrys, that's a completely different market. People buy cars based on affordability, reliability and what suits the local market. India's domestic automotive manufacturing industry and its contribution to global automotive supply chains are substantial. Comparing car preferences in Australia with those in India doesn't really make the point you think it does.
